title: Closed immersions on affine opens: surjective ring maps, and the criterion by an affine open covering of the target
statement: Let $h:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]; for an open $V\subseteq S$ write $h^\sharp_V:\mathcal O_S(V)\to\mathcal O_X(h^{-1}(V))$ for the ring map induced by $h$. (1) If $h$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], then for every affine open $V\subseteq S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] the open subscheme $h^{-1}(V)\subseteq X$ is affine and $h^\sharp_V$ is surjective. (2) Conversely, if $S=\bigcup_{j\in J}V_j$ is a covering by affine opens such that for every $j$ the open subscheme $h^{-1}(V_j)$ is affine and $h^\sharp_{V_j}$ is surjective, then $h$ is a closed immersion. (Stacks Morphisms, Lemma 01QO, (1)$\Rightarrow$(2) and (3)$\Rightarrow$(1): for affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and affine $h^{-1}(V)$, '$h^{-1}(V)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ over $V$ for an ideal $I$' is the same as '$h^\sharp_V$ surjective', with $I=\ker h^\sharp_V$.)
